analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, all patches, the changelog head and supplied inference-documentation base excerpts. changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md:3 and docs/architecture/inference.md head:810–813 document newly accepted variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks, presentation-order indexing and synthetic timestamps using nominalFrameRate; head:829 removes VFR from deterministic refusals. These are documentation changes, not evidence of an observed missing runtime control, so no concrete regression is supported in this batch.
The patch retains the documented 2 FPS sampler, 512 MiB retained decoded-frame cap, shared visual-token cap, media memory reservation and exclusion from prefix lookup/capture (T-041, A-001, TB-007). No supplied change modifies authorization/attestation, hop encryption, credentials, billing or privileged-helper behavior. The surrounding native ownership, memory admission and managed-loading descriptions are unchanged and are not independently verified here.
Integration should inspect GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and the VFR tests: accepting irregular timestamps must preserve finite/positive rate validation, bounded source-frame decoding (not just retained RGB bytes), duration/frame-count consistency, cancellation and decode-time limits. VFR acceptance expands consumer-controlled decoder inputs; the implementation is absent from this batch, so resource safety remains unverified rather than a finding. Also confirm existing in-memory media handling remains intact under T-050 and token budgeting still bounds the generated sample spans. These questions concern the changed media path, not unrelated unchanged dependencies.
